title: Nissan’s Z Kaze Concept Is a T-Topped Tuner Throwback

body_markdown:
Nissan unveiled the tuner-inspired Z Kaze concept at ZCON, the annual meeting of the Z Car Club Association, held this year in Phoenix. ”Kaze” is the Japanese word for wind, and while there’s no longer a drop-top Z in the lineup, Nissan went with the next best thing: T-tops. According to Nissan, the design team was “guided by a vision of an exhilarating drive along California’s Pacific Coast Highway on a perfect summer day.” With its added performance and grip, as well as lots of retro style, the Z Kaze looks ready for PCH or any other curvy road that beckons.


Larry Chen


“The Z Kaze concept celebrates some of Nissan’s most iconic open-top sports cars, while recognizing the ’90s tuning culture that helped put Nissan and[NISMO](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/nissans-manual-equipped-z-nismo-starts-under-70k/) on the map,” said Ponz Pandikuthira, senior vice president, chief product and planning officer, Nissan Americas. “This passion project combines Nissan’s engineering excellence, creativity, and celebration of the brand’s heritage.”


The carbon fiber flares and body kit are emphasized by the lowered stance provided by a NISMO suspension.


Larry Chen


Nissan embraced tuner car culture by adding a carbon fiber body kit, fender flares, and a vented hood. The wider bodywork demanded something special, so the Z Kaze received a vintage set of 18-inch NISMO LMGT2 wheels. Long out of production, the set was rebuilt wider and better than ever. The 10-inch-wide front wheels and 11-inch-wide rear wheels are finished in white with a polished lip. A slightly lowered stance, appropriate for the more aggressive bodywork and wider wheels, is courtesy of NISMO suspension parts.


Larry Chen


Larry Chen


Occupants can enjoy the wind in their hair and still hear the audio system, thanks to Bose Personal Plus headrest speakers.


Some of the other nostalgic touches employed in the Z Kaze include its Pacific Teal paint. No other car color better represents the decade, and this hue serves as a great contrast to the white wheels and rocker graphics. The accents continue inside the Z Kaze, as the white leather seats add to the openness provided by the glass T-tops. The interior also features a few select bits of carbon fiber trim to match the exterior.


Larry Chen


Larry Chen


The Z Kaze embraces the Z’s long history of factory performance, as well as serving as a canvas for the aftermarket to expand on. Not afraid to show that there’s even more beyond the NISMO parts catalog, Nissan partnered with a few aftermarket companies on the build, including Greddy. The Z’s 3.0-liter twin-turbo V-6 breathes even better thanks to a Greddy Airinx air filter kit, front-mounted charge cooler, and Supreme SP Exhaust.


The concept will remain on display at ZCON through September 26. After that, you can catch it in person at the[Japanese Classic Car Show](https://japaneseclassiccarshow.com/) in Long Beach, California, on October 3.
